<reason>CON (A) built and sustained a single decisive frame—the "trilemma"—that intelligence precise enough to justify an authorized search zone is precise enough to generate individualized suspicion under existing law, and if it isn't, the power is by definition a dragnet on people with zero indicators. PRO (B) never cleanly escaped this: its operational-level-grounds distinction (threat established at a place/time without identifying carriers) is a real conceptual attempt, but A's repeated rejoinder—"the carrier is indistinguishable from everyone else in the zone, so the only way to search them is to search everyone"—landed and was never squarely answered beyond restating that boundaries remain "challengeable." A also pressed a timing asymmetry that mattered for weighing: trust damage happens immediately at authorization, while B's revocation/review safeguards only bite after cumulative harm is measured, making correction structurally too late to undo the cooperation loss the whole preventive theory depends on. B's replies ("both sides carry uncertain harms," "communities deserve restraint without enforced helplessness") were reasonable but didn't neutralize this asymmetry or the trilemma; they mostly re-asserted the value of a bounded exception without dismantling why that exception collapses into either redundancy or a dragnet. Both sides handled the Pressure Questions format correctly (A1/A2 labels, correct ordering), which is a wash on execution, but A's opening was clipped for exceeding the word limit, a real cost that slightly tempers its case. Even so, across rebuttals and closing, A sharpened the central clash more effectively and left B's key distinction structurally unresolved, giving A the cleaner path to a decision.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>A's turn 4 (A2.3–A2.5) and turn 8 (A4.1–A4.4), pressing the trilemma that intelligence sharp enough for an operation is sharp enough for individualized suspicion under current law, forced B into a distinction (operation-level grounds vs. person-level grounds) that B could assert but never fully defend against the "search everyone in the zone" collapse.</best_rebuttal>
